name: W25Q32
full_name: Winbond W25Q32JV 32Mbit (4M x 8) Serial SPI NOR Flash Memory
description: The W25Q32JV is a 32 Mbit (4 MB) serial NOR flash memory supporting standard SPI, Dual SPI, and Quad SPI on a single 8-pin package. It runs at 2.7V-3.6V with clocks up to 133 MHz and is organized into 64 KB blocks, 4 KB sectors, and 256-byte program pages. With QE set in Status Register-2, the /WP and /HOLD pins become IO2 and IO3 for quad I/O. Endurance is 100,000 program/erase cycles per sector with 20-year retention. Its standout trait is being the ubiquitous low-cost SPI flash for firmware/QSPI XIP storage on ESP32, RP2040, and countless dev boards.

pins.name: /CS
pins.description: chip select, active low; high tristates DO and puts device in standby

pins.name: DO (IO1)
pins.description: data output in standard SPI; IO1 in dual/quad mode

pins.name: /WP (IO2)
pins.description: write protect (active low) in SPI; becomes IO2 when quad enable is set

pins.name: DI (IO0)
pins.description: data input in standard SPI; IO0 in dual/quad mode

pins.name: /HOLD (IO3)
pins.description: hold (active low), pauses device while selected; becomes IO3 when quad enable is set (may be /RESET on some packages)

typical_application: External firmware/code (XIP via QSPI), filesystem, or asset storage for microcontrollers like ESP32 and RP2040.
gotchas: 3.3V part only; applying 5V will damage it, level-shift if driving from a 5V MCU
in standard SPI you must keep /WP and /HOLD high (or tie to VCC) or the device stalls; many designs hardwire them high
Quad mode reuses /WP as IO2 and /HOLD as IO3 only after the Quad Enable (QE) bit in Status Register-2 is set
program pages are 256 bytes and writes wrap within the page; erase is sector (4 KB) or block granularity, you cannot byte-erase
dedicated /RESET only exists on SOIC-16/TFBGA packages; on SOIC-8 pin 7 is /HOLD or /RESET-as-IO3, not an independent reset
/CS needs a pull-up so it stays high during MCU reset/power-up to avoid spurious commands
